stories.headline: IAF helicopter makes emergency landing in Karnataka's Haveri
stories.bodyText: Haveri: An Indian Air Force helicopter made an emergency landing in an agricultural field at Kamanahalli village in Shiggaon taluk of Haveri district on Wednesday following a technical malfunction. . The helicopter, bearing registration number ZD 4050, was carrying six personnel, including the pilot, when the technical snag developed mid-flight. Sensing potential danger, the pilot decided to make an emergency landing in a field near Kamanahalli, alongside the National Highway. .Training aircraft makes emergency landing on agricultural land in Karnataka's Kalaburagi . The helicopter was travelling from Sulur in Tamil Nadu to Belagavi. The crew was operating under the leadership of Air Force personnel Deepak Sharma. . Fortunately, all six occupants escaped unharmed, and no casualties were reported. . Shiggaon police visited the spot and inspected the helicopter following the incident.

stories.headline: New Entrepreneurship Centre inauguration on Nov 14: DC Ikram Sharif
stories.deck: New Entrepreneurship Centre inauguration on Nov 14: DC
stories.bodyText: Kalaburagi: Deputy Commissioner Ikram Sharif said that the inauguration of the New Entrepreneurship Centre and ‘Kalyana Karnataka Startup Dialogue’ will be held on November 14. . Addressing a press conference here on Thursday, DC said the aim is to expand the IT-BT and startup sectors beyond Bengaluru. It has been decided to develop Kalaburagi into a key hub for regional startups under the state government’s ambitious ‘LEAP’ initiative. . Stating that a ‘Centre of Excellence’ for rural innovation and agricultural startups has been established through the Krushikalpa Foundation, he said a grant of approximately Rs 12 to Rs 12.5 crore has been provided for this project. . He added that the government is taking steps to support startups by providing essential mentorship, networking opportunities, and assistance in raising capital. . The government plans to establish ‘LEAP Labs’— a state-of-the-art co-working space near the High Court— and is moving forward with constructing a well-equipped IT Park in the vicinity of the city, he added. . KrushiKalpa Foundation CEO C M Patil said the inauguration of the new premises of the incubation centre will be held on November 14. . The Kalyana Karnataka Startup Dialogue-2026 is being organised for the first time, centred on themes of exploring new entrepreneurial possibilities beyond Bengaluru and showcasing the entrepreneurial potential of the Kalyana Karnataka region. . The event will take place at the KrushiKalpa Foundation in Kalaburagi from 9.30 am to 6 pm, DC Sharif added. . 300 startups . More than 300 registered startups, entrepreneurs, angel investors, venture capitalists, industry leaders, and policymakers from the seven districts of the Kalyana Karnataka region— Kalaburagi, Bidar, Raichur, Yadgir, Koppal, Ballari, and Vijayanagara— will converge on this platform. A special ‘Solvathon’ initiative has been organised in collaboration with the local administration. This initiative allows students to apply their skills to develop practical solutions for real-world challenges faced by government departments, he explained. . Prominent leaders . He also said prominent industry leaders from across the country, including Vipul Mittal of BigBasket, Adarsh Srivastava of DeHaat, Sachin Nandwana of BigHaat, Dr Taslimarif Saiyed (Director of C-CAMP), and Sanjeev Gupta (CEO of KDEM), will participate in the event. . The primary objective of this initiative is to create a supportive ecosystem that enables young people to build successful enterprises locally, thereby preventing the need for them to migrate to major metropolitan cities in search of employment, he added.

stories.headline: U.S., Ukraine say Europe to join Russia talks as Putin sticks to hardline stance
stories.deck: U.S. envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin
stories.bodyText:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said Thursday (November 12, 2026) Europe would join the next round of talks with Russia, as Vladimir Putin indicated Moscow will not compromise on its hardline demands to end almost five years of war.
In a packed day of shuttle diplomacy following negotiations in Abu Dhabi, Mr. Kushner and fellow envoy Steve Witkoff held over four hours of talks with Mr. Putin in the Kremlin before jetting to debrief Mr. Zelenskyy in Dublin.
As they spoke to journalists on the tarmac of a military airbase in Ireland, the main piece of progress touted by the Ukrainian leader and U.S. President Donald Trump's representative was that European negotiators would be at the table for future talks.
Mr. Zelenskyy said Europeans will take part rather than remain "separately" on the sidelines as they were in Abu Dhabi, insisting: "They will have a voice".
Mr. Kushner later reiterated the sentiment in a post on X, writing: "Both sides have now agreed to expand the next round of negotiations to include our European partners."
"Significant differences remain, but we are encouraged by the progress made," he posted, adding that the schedule and details on the negotiating track would be released "shortly".
An EU official told AFP representatives of five European capitals as well as the European Commission that the U.S. envoys, and that a new multilateral meeting "will be fixed soon".
The Kremlin did not confirm Mr. Putin had agreed to include Europe in future talks, which Kyiv and its allies have long been seeking.
Instead, the Russian leader had earlier told the U.S. duo he would not water down demands to control parts of Ukraine that Russia claims to have annexed and ruled out agreeing to foreign peacekeeping troops in Ukraine -- a deployment he said would be a "continuation of war".
Mr. Putin's comments appeared to douse hopes a peace deal could be getting nearer.
As the United States has pushed for Europe to be allowed at the table, Moscow has sought to reframe talks as part of a wider discussion about European security.
Kyiv and European leaders have insisted there is no need to rewrite the arrangements underpinning the continent's security, and said Russia must first stop hostilities.
In the Irish capital for a summit of European leaders, Mr. Zelenskyy, meanwhile, said fresh restrictions on the Starshield satellite internet service were hampering Ukraine's ability to intercept Russia's jet-drones, meaning "more of our people are killed".
No 'grey' zones
Usually held behind closed doors, the Kremlin chose to televise a lengthy opening exchange between Putin and the U.S. envoys.
The Russian leader rejected talk of a possible territorial settlement involving "grey" -- or demilitarised -- zones between Ukrainian and Russian positions.
"For us, there is only one line of demarcation: the state border. Because then it will be clear: here are we, and here are you," he said.
Russia has seized swathes of eastern and southern Ukraine since launching its full-scale offensive in 2022, in addition to Crimea, which it annexed in 2014, and territory that was under the control of Russian-backed separatists.
Moscow has formally annexed four Ukrainian regions -- Donetsk, Kherson, Lugansk and Zaporizhzhia -- despite not having full control over them, annexations rejected by Kyiv and the West as illegal.
Mr. Putin proposed organising what he called a "humanitarian mission" to the city of Kostyantynivka, where he said some 400-500 civilians still lived.
Russia claimed in the summer to have captured the city, but Ukraine insists fighting there is ongoing.
The idea would be modelled on a short-term truce that last month allowed hundreds of stranded locals to flee the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine.
Dmytro Lytvyn, an adviser to Ukraine's Zelenskyy, warned Russia would try to rotate in new troops "under the cover of a humanitarian operation".
Mr. Putin also repeated his long-standing objection to any foreign troops being deployed to Ukraine as a post-war peacekeeping force -- saying Moscow would see any such deployment a "legitimate target".
United vision
European countries have been rattled by Russia pushing a review of the entire continent's security architecture, with the United States also floating a new framework.
That is widely seen as a reference to Moscow's long-standing demands to push back the NATO military alliance in eastern Europe and end Western military support to Kyiv.
Russia and the United States have also been pushing Europe to name a single representative they can deal with.
As European leaders gathered in Dublin, EU chief Antonio Costa said "there is no need to reinvent the wheel" on Europe's security framework as he accused Russia of wrecking it by attacking Ukraine.
In a French-backed declaration, 39 countries insisted "any matter affecting European security should be decided with the Europeans".

stories.headline: Microsoft 365 outage drags on as company observes ‘limited recovery’
stories.deck: A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa
stories.bodyText:
Microsoft Outlook suffered a major outage across the world Thursday (November 12, 2026), with tens of thousands of users struggling to access their email as the company said it was working "aggressively" to reduce the impact.
The disruption, which Microsoft attributed to "elevated load" on its infrastructure, dragged on for much of the U.S. workday and also affected other company products such as Teams and the AI assistant Copilot.
The disruption went global within a span of an hour, knocking out Microsoft products in 74 countries and territories, outage tracker Downdetector reported.
A map posted by Downdetector on X showed the outage affected users across the Americas, and parts of Europe, Asia and Africa.
Microsoft initially said it was investigating outage reports "in the Americas," but later confirmed that the issue apparently affected "Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region."
Microsoft 365 is the company's cloud-based subscription service that includes popular applications such as Outlook and Teams.
"We've determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors," the company wrote on X.
"We're aggressively pursuing all pathways to reduce impact," it added.
"We've paused all deployments, we're moving additional traffic off the affected infrastructure, and we're restarting affected servers to return them to service."
In the United States, around 130,000 users reported issues with Outlook shortly after 1 pm Eastern Time (1800 GMT), according to Downdetector.
Outage reports have since declined, with about 37,000 users reporting experiencing issues with Outlook as of 6 pm Eastern Time (2300 GMT).
Thousands of users also reported issues with Teams and Copilot, according to Downdetector.
As the outage dragged on for hours, Microsoft posted a series of updates on X, detailing continued but unsuccessful efforts to restore full service.
In one update shortly after 6 pm Eastern Time, Microsoft said it was "observing limited recovery" as it sought to route user traffic away from affected servers.
"As capacity is restored, users may experience a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect," the company added.

stories.headline: DC gym shooting: Shooter complained about mould, water damage in apartment before attacking
stories.deck: Shooting incidents occurred in a Washington DC gym where Dr. Matt Lambert opened fire, killing the building manager. Witnesses described scenes of chaos and horror during the attack. Lambert had expressed grievances over issues in his apartment prior to the shooting. He had been involved in a lawsuit against the condominium association regarding alleged damages. The shooting ended with Lambert…
stories.bodyText:
A man who opened fire at a gym inside a luxury condominium building in Washington DC, killing the building manager and injuring four others, had repeatedly complained about mould and water damage in his apartment before the shooting, police said.
The gunman, identified as 55-year-old Dr Matt Lambert, later shot himself inside his apartment following a standoff with police. Three firearms were recovered from the apartment, according to law enforcement sources cited by CBS News.
The shooting took place on Thursday morning at the Vida Fitness centre on the ground floor of the Metropole Condominiums in the Logan Circle neighbourhood. Police identified the person killed as 46-year-old James Stuart, who managed the building.
An X account under the name @OfMiceandMold, which CBS News linked to Lambert, contained dozens of posts detailing his grievances over alleged disrepair in his apartment.
He had repeatedly criticised the building's contractors and property management company, EJF Real Estate Services, accusing them of failing to address problems with his unit.
'My manifesto is an engineering report'
Shortly before the shooting, Lambert posted what he described as an engineering report examining mould and water-related problems in the building.
"My manifesto is an engineering report," he wrote on X.
In an October 1 post, he appeared to refer to the 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare chief executive Brian Thompson by Luigi Mangione. Lambert wrote: "After months of 'Luigi' tactics (delay, deny, defend) by the HOA, we were finally able to submit an independent engineering report into the record."
He also said he would share the report on X "when the time is right".
In another social media post dated April 28, Lambert wrote, "If you're looking for the building manager, I would check the gym."
Lambert had filed a lawsuit against the Metropole Condominium Association, alleging damages of more than $290,000 as of May. The association and EJF denied responsibility, arguing that any damage had been caused by third parties beyond their control and that Lambert had failed to limit his losses.
Witnesses describe chaos during shooting
Police said Lambert opened fire inside the building's gym before returning to his apartment, where he remained during a standoff with officers and eventually killed himself.
A woman who was exercising on a treadmill when the shooting began told CBS News that she had to evacuate by passing the area where one of the victims had been killed.
"There was no way of getting out of the gym other than going past that scene," she said.
"It was like chaos. It was horrific, honestly."
Another witness, who lived directly below Lambert and was about 20 feet from the shooting, said the suspect had become increasingly upset during homeowners' association meetings. He said Lambert had previously invited residents into his apartment to show them the condition of the unit.
The witness described the 99-unit condominium as a "tight-knit community". During the shooting and police standoff, his girlfriend barricaded herself inside their apartment. He said the flat was subsequently left under an inch of water following the firefighting response.
Doctor had bought penthouse for $1.1 million
Lambert had purchased the condominium in September 2016 for $1,095,000, according to Washington DC tax records. Court documents showed that he owned a penthouse unit in the building.
He ran MLEM, a healthcare and technology consultancy, and had studied medicine at Marshall University in West Virginia before completing his residency at West Virginia University, according to his LinkedIn profile.
As per his personal website, Lambert is described as a board-certified emergency physician with more than two decades of clinical experience. The website also said he had volunteered in underserved communities in Kenya, Belize and Haiti.
The shooting took place in the Logan Circle neighbourhood, where the Vida Fitness centre catered to residents of the condominium building. Police have identified the building manager as the person killed in the attack, while four others were wounded.

briefs.headline: Shivamogga airport to be classified as ‘underserved’
briefs.deck: S’mogga airport to be classified as ‘underserved’
briefs.bodyText: Shivamogga: Karnataka State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation Chairman S G Nanjayyanamath said that commercial flight services from Shivamogga airport would be discontinued from November 21 following the expiry of the agreement period under the UDAN scheme. However, efforts are being made to resume flight services within three to four months, he added. . Speaking to reporters here on Thursday, he said that airline operators had proposed discontinuing services from November 21 as the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) facility provided under the UDAN framework was coming to an end. There are concerns that, without scheduled commercial flight operations, Shivamogga airport could be relegated to the status of an ‘underserved airport’. . He explained that air connectivity through Shivamogga airport was essential for the economic, tourism and educational development of the Malnad region and its neighbouring districts, including Chikkamagaluru, Uttara Kannada, Davanagere and Haveri. A request had been submitted to the Ministry of Civil Aviation seeking special consideration for 13 new routes proposed from Shivamogga airport under the revised RCS-UDAN 6.0 scheme. . He also mentioned that flight services in several locations, including Shivamogga, Bengaluru, Mysuru, Hubballi, Kalaburagi and Belagavi, had faced disruptions or, in some cases, complete suspension following the expiry of the three-year agreement to operate flights under the UDAN scheme. Efforts were now underway to extend the agreement, he said. . He said that to ensure the continuation of air services and extension of the agreement period, the state government had approached the concerned Union ministers and senior officials with a formal request. Since the scheme involves an 80% contribution from the Centre and a 20% contribution from the state government, approval from the Centre was currently awaited. The Centre had been urged to take immediate and appropriate action to prevent further inconvenience to passengers. The matter had also been brought to the attention of the MP, who had expressed interest in the issue. . Regarding the night-landing facility, he said the work was almost complete, with only a few minor tasks remaining, which were expected to be completed within a few months. A specialised aircraft was scheduled to arrive from Bengaluru for flight calibration. A team of experts would conduct the calibration and submit a report. Following this, the report would be presented to the government, after which the facility would be commissioned, he explained. . He also mentioned that all 80 employees currently working at the airport were being retained and were receiving their salaries regularly. Furthermore, necessary steps were being taken to provide compensation to farmers who had given up their land for the airport. Nanjayyanamath assured that there were no major administrative hurdles concerning the airport and that all issues would be resolved as soon as possible. . District Congress Committee president H C Yogesh, Airport Director Shamanth and KSISF Assistant Commandant Shashikumar Naik were present.

briefs.headline: Centre invests Rs 7,250 crore in magnet manufacturing scheme
briefs.deck: ‘Centre invests Rs 7,250 crore in magnet manufacturing scheme’
briefs.bodyText: Tumakuru: The Union government has launched the Rare Earth Permanent Magnet (REPM) scheme with an outlay of Rs 7,250 crore to promote domestic manufacturing of magnets and reduce dependence on imports, said Union Minister H D Kumaraswamy. . Speaking after performing the bhumipuja for the manufacturing unit of Adarsh Chemicals at the Japan Township in Vasanthanarasapura Industrial Area on the outskirts of Tumakuru on Thursday, he said China accounted for nearly 90% of global magnet production. Following China’s decision to stop supplying magnets to India, the Centre introduced the REPM scheme under the ‘Make in India’ initiative. . The scheme would support manufacturing industries, particularly electric vehicles and the defence sector, by ensuring the availability of permanent magnets locally, he said. . Kumaraswamy said attracting industries to a state was primarily the responsibility of its government and not the Centre. The Union Ministry of Industries was responsible for introducing Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes to encourage industrial growth. Under these schemes, the Centre had so far released Rs 11,500 crore in incentives to industries across various states. . Pointing to the industrial incentives offered by other states, he said Andhra Pradesh provided a 50% subsidy to an entrepreneur investing Rs 100 crore in setting up an industrial unit. Odisha and Tamil Nadu were also offering incentives to attract investments. . Providing infrastructure and creating a conducive environment for industries were the responsibilities of state governments. They should take the initiative to attract entrepreneurs and facilitate investments, he said. . Adarsh Chemicals Managing Director G S Omkarmurthy said the Union Minister’s visit would encourage the growth of local industries. Nearly 90% of the employees at the company’s unit were from the local area. The company was also undertaking social development activities under its corporate social responsibility (CSR) programme. . Sting operation . Later, speaking to reporters, Kumaraswamy said it remained to be seen whom the police would give a clean chit to in the sting operation involving former chief minister Siddaramaiah, whether Krupa Alva or someone else. . An investigation into the sting operation was under way, and it was unnecessary to discuss the matter further until the reasons behind it came to light, he said. . Kumaraswamy also criticised Chief Minister D K Shivakumar for repeatedly accusing him of lying. Referring to the Cabinet meeting held in Mangaluru, he questioned the announcement of projects worth Rs 32,000 crore for Dakshina Kannada district and asked whether the state government had the financial resources to implement them. . On whether the Congress high command was restricting Shivakumar’s functioning, he said the Chief Minister should understand how to discharge his responsibilities instead of merely making statements. He claimed to have demonstrated how a Chief Minister should function and challenged Shivakumar to do the same. . Responding to Congress leaders’ allegations that he had done little for Karnataka as a Union Minister, Kumaraswamy said attracting industries was the responsibility of the state government, while his role was to secure central incentives and schemes to promote industrial development. . On the proposed Hiriyur Assembly bypoll, he said JD(S) and BJP leaders would jointly decide whether to field a candidate. Discussions were also under way on an alliance for the Zilla Panchayat and Taluk Panchayat elections, he added.

briefs.headline: Found an animal in distress? Here’s who you can call
briefs.deck: Found an animal in distress? Here’s who you can call
briefs.bodyText: Spotted an injured dog, a bird struggling to fly, or an abandoned kitten in your neighbourhood? This may be quite a common sight during and after the festive season, when firecrackers and loud noises take a toll on animals. Here is who to call for help. . Dogs and cats . Charlie’s Animal Rescue Centre (CARE), Yelahanka, can accommodate around 180 injured dogs and has nine vehicles that patrol the city, responding to emergency calls. “We focus on bringing in injured animals, treating them, and then releasing them back at the same location where they are found,” says centre manager Keerthan R P. The centre receives 150 calls on average daily. . Call: 81230 38270 . CUPA (Compassion Unlimited Plus Action) runs a Trauma and Rescue Centre on Bellary Road for injured and distressed community animals, including dogs. Accidents, old age, and maggot wounds are among the top causes for distress. The centre does not have a long-term shelter for animals post-recovery. “We get about 40-45 calls a day, out of which we have to choose the most important calls since there is a space restriction,” says Suparna Ganguly, co-founder and trustee, CUPA. The trauma care centre cannot accommodate more than 75 animals. . For details, visit cupabangalore.org .Activists flag poor conditions at north Bengaluru dog shelter. Friend For Animal Trust, an NGO based in Avalahalli, offers treatment for injured dogs, alongside permanent residency for old, blind, and vulnerable dogs. “We ask reporters for a video, a current location pin, and a point of contact,” says Vikash A Bafna, founder. The shelter houses over 400 dogs. Of those, 200 are permanent residents. . Call: 81476 20003 . Praana Cat Rehabilitation and Adoption Center, Yelachenahalli, collaborates with veterinary clinics for medical aid. The centre can accommodate 45 cats and the team picks up rescue calls from all over the city, with three ambulances for strays. “We also rescue dogs, but send them to different NGOs or facilities for treatment and care,” says Aniruddha Ravindra, managing director of Praana. Once treated, the centre facilitates rehabilitation through adoption. . Call: 91088 19998 . Birds and reptiles . To rescue injured birds, reptiles (snakes, monitor lizards), and mammals (palm civets, mongooses, bats, squirrels), one can contact People for Animal’s (PFA) Wildlife Hospital in Kengeri. “Don’t fear, harm, or abandon injured animals. Their survival increasingly depends on how we coexist responsibly,” says chief wildlife veterinarian Dr Navaz Shariff. . Call: 99000 25370 . The Pigeon Hospital, run by Shree Shankheswar Parshwanath Jain Kabootar Daana Seva Samithi, Rajajinagar, treats 50-60 injured pigeons everyday. “While we don’t have transportation, we request people to send the injured birds in a cab,” says trustee and founding member Vasanthraj Ranka. . Call: 98452 21309

stories.headline: This Children’s Day, let the kids call the shots
stories.deck: From cracking internet slang and trading dance steps to swapping mall arcades for lake trails, here is how Bengaluru parents are reclaiming genuine connection this weekend
stories.bodyText:
Children's Day
 usually arrives wrapped in familiar tropes: school skits, quick mall runs, and token toy purchases. But for urban parents navigating packed work weeks and competing screen timers, November 14 is increasingly becoming a reason for a reset — not by over-programming the calendar, but by letting children set the agenda.Whether that means a parent attempting viral choreography in the living room or families trading air-conditioned gaming zones for lakeside bug-hunting, here is how to make this weekend count:
Surrender the aux cord and the slang
Most modern parents spend their days trying to decode what their children are consuming online. This weekend, lean into the chaos. Step away from the supervisory role and let your child become the tutor, whether they are teaching you a choreography challenge, decoding schoolyard internet slang, or making you sit through their current obsession without commentary.
"My thirteen-year-old speaks in what feels like another language half the time," laughs Tanishq, a father to a teenager. "Between trending slang and K-Pop references, I’m usually completely lost. So this Children’s Day, my assignment is simple: sit down, let her build my Spotify playlist, and attempt whatever dance step she's currently obsessing over. If I embarrass myself, that’s half the fun," he says.
Swap the mall arcade for living history
The default family outing often ends up in a noisy indoor play zone. Bengaluru, however, offers far richer sensory escapes if you step slightly off the beaten track. Take a walk under the bamboo groves at Cubbon Park before the traffic sets in, spend an afternoon untangling the mechanics of sound at the Indian Music Experience in JP Nagar, or trace old fortress stone at Tipu Sultan’s Summer Palace.
"It’s easy to slip into standard weekend autopilot where everyone is physically present but glued to a device," says Namita S, mother to a 10-year-old. "We’re skipping the usual food court routine this time. We’re making pancakes at home, pulling out art supplies with zero rules on mess, and heading out for an old-fashioned park picnic," she says.
Get messy, together
Children rarely remember the gadgets bought for them; they remember the shared mess. Pick a project where neither of you is an expert, whether it’s failing at rolling out dough together, hand-building lumpy pottery mugs, or attempting a DIY science kit on the dining table. When parents are willing to be beginners alongside their kids, the dynamic shifts from instruction to camaraderie.
Where to take the kids in Bengaluru this weekend
From storytelling sessions and creative workshops to nature walks, costume carnivals, and family sports activities, here are 10 curated events across town:
1. Block Party! A two-day celebration featuring open construction and free-play zones, sensory corners, arts and crafts, and storytelling sessions.
Age group: All ages
When: November 13 and 14, 11 am – 6 pm
Where: Sabha, Shivajinagar
2. Po’Purrie
A programme of performances, workshops, and short films for young audiences. Highlights include Neer (an interactive experience for ages 2–5) and Mister Jeejeebhoy & the Birds (ages 5–12), alongside puppet-making, soundscapes, movement, and storytelling.
Age group: 2–12 years
When: November 13, 11 am - 5 pm

stories.headline: Mischievous accounting, Karnataka manufactured 84% lie: MP Surya
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A day after the Congress govt claimed the Centre’s share in capital infusion for 
Bangalore Metro
 project plummeted to 16% over years, BJP Thursday argued the 84% figure was arrived at by wrongly counting BMRCL loans as the state’s contribution.
Ahead of the inauguration of Namma Metro’s 7.5-km elevated Pink Line stretch between Kalena Agrahara and Suddaguntepalya by PM Modi on Friday, BJP claimed the financing pattern for Bangalore Metro is 54:46, contrary to Congress govt’s 84:16 calculation.
Bangalore South MP 
Tejasvi Surya
 accused the Congress govt of indulging in ‘credit chori’ and alleged nearly Rs 29,000 crore in foreign loans provided to BMRCL by international financial institutions, backed by the Centre’s sovereign guarantee, had been included in the state’s contribution to project Karnataka govt’s share as substantially higher.
“This money is routed to BMRCL, which is also responsible for repaying loans. Where is the state govt’s contribution to this? They are misleading the public through mischievous accounting,” Surya said.
BJP’s response came after Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda stated that of the total Namma Metro project cost of Rs 77,891 crore, the state govt had contributed Rs 65,291 crore, while the Centre’s contribution stood at Rs 12,600 crore.
Surya argued BMRCL, a special purpose vehicle, was a separate entity and its borrowings should not be treated as direct state govt expenditure.
Excluding loans from the state’s contribution, its share would fall to 46.6%, while the remaining 53.4% would include Centre-backed institutional financing and other funding, Surya claimed.
On the state govt bearing expenses towards land acquisition, rehabilitation, grants-in-aid and other components, Surya said these were part of the agreed funding arrangements and were not exclusive to Karnataka.
On the proposed Red line (Sarjapur-Hebbal), Surya rejected the state govt’s charge that the Centre had delayed approval for more than 22 months. He said the Centre had scrutinised the detailed project report and reduced the proposed cost from Rs 28,405 crore to Rs 25,999 crore, resulting in a saving of Rs 2,406 crore.
On Orange line, Surya accused the state govt of delaying implementation by repeatedly changing the design.
Surya said the elevated corridor of Pink line had received central approval in 2014, but the then Congress govt awarded the construction contract only in 2017.
You stop my speech, but you can’t stop my work: KBG
Pink line Metro trial runs on Bannerghatta road ahead of its inauguration. The elevated section of the line, connecting Kalena Agrahara to Tavarekere, will open for commercial services on Nov 14
Greater Bengaluru development minister Krishna Byre Gowda Thursday alleged he had been denied an opportunity to speak at the Pink line inauguration at the IIMB auditorium because he demanded justice for Karnataka.
The minister was referring to a skewed Centre-state contribution to Namma Metro projects.
On X, he said, “You may cut my speech, but you cannot stop me from working for Bengaluru’s development. We’ll continue our work with even greater commitment.”
Byre Gowda said his speech, included in the draft programme, was excised late night.
According to the final programme schedule, 
PM Narendra Modi
, governor Sudha Yadav, chief minister DK Shivakumar and Bangalore South MP Tejasvi Surya will address the gathering.
The PM is scheduled to travel by Metro from Suddaguntepalya to IIMB before inaugurating the 7.5-km elevated Pink line stretch and launching several other projects.

briefs.headline: Karnataka sets Rs 7.5 lakh crore investment target for 2027-30; Global Investors Meet from April 20
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: 
Karnataka
 has set an ambitious target of attracting investments worth Rs 7.5 lakh crore and generating 20 lakh jobs by 2030, with the next edition of the Global Investors Meet (GIM) scheduled to be held at Bengaluru’s Palace Grounds from April 20 to 22, 2027.
Announcing the dates at the curtain-raiser event on Thursday, industries minister M B Patil said the govt was preparing to make the three-day event a truly global initiative, with a series of international outreach programmes to take Karnataka’s investment opportunities directly to investors in their respective countries and markets. As part of the preparations, govt unveiled the Aerospace and Defence Policy 2026-31 and launched the KIADB Digital Industrial Land Bank along with the third edition of VentuRISE.
“Although the digital land bank and VentuRISE initiatives serve different purposes, they complement each other. One focuses on building the companies of tomorrow, while the other makes it easier to establish those businesses today. Together, these initiatives capture the central idea behind the Global Investors Meet 2027 — backing ambition with effective implementation,” Patil said.
Highlighting the progress made since the previous GIM in 2025, he said Karnataka had received investment commitments worth approximately Rs 10.27 lakh crore, exceeding govt’s expectations. 
Around 65% of the manufacturing investments had already been converted into projects, with land allotments, approvals and construction progressing across the state. “The real measure of the success of an investors’ meet is not the day the MoUs are signed, but the day the factories begin operations,” he said.
Investments by companies such as DN Solutions, Krones, Nidec and Foxconn had become operational in record time, while major projects by Lam Research, Applied Materials, MV, Wipro Electronic Materials, Jindal Aluminium and Mahindra Aerospace were progressing. The govt will also organise a dedicated investors’ conclave in North Karnataka to showcase opportunities in Kalyana Karnataka and Kittur Karnataka regions. “We want these regions to attract investments on a scale they have never witnessed before,” he said.
Chief minister 
D K Shivakumar
, inviting domestic and international investors to partner with Karnataka, said the state was positioning itself as a leading destination for semiconductors, aerospace, space technology, artificial intelligence, clean energy, life sciences and electric mobility. “This is not just an investment summit. It is an opportunity to shape Karnataka’s future. Bring your ideas. Bring your investments. We will build the future together,” he said.
Highlighting the state’s economic performance, Shivakumar said Karnataka’s economy grew by 8% last year, outperforming the national growth rate. The state had the highest per capita income among India’s major states and the second-highest GST collections after Maharashtra. Karnataka attracted nearly USD 13 billion in foreign direct investment last year and is home to more than 1,100 global capability centres (GCCs), the highest in the country. It contributes over 40% of India’s software exports, while nearly two-thirds of the country’s aerospace exports originate from the state, he said.
Under the Industrial Policy 2025-30, govt has set the target of attracting Rs 7.5 lakh crore in investments and creating 20 lakh jobs. The Aerospace and Defence Policy 2026-31 aims to attract Rs 60,000 crore and generate 60,000 jobs, while the Textile and Apparel Policy 2026-31 targets Rs 20,000 crore in investments and five lakh jobs.
To encourage industries in backward regions, eligible units will receive additional incentives, including capital subsidies of up to 20% in the most backward and priority taluks. Shivakumar said the next phase of Karnataka’s economic growth would extend beyond Bengaluru to Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi, Tumakuru and Kalaburagi. 
Govt is promoting at least five industrial and innovation clusters outside Bengaluru, besides strengthening industrial parks, roads, logistics and regional connectivity.
On infrastructure, he said the 2026-27 state budget had earmarked Rs 84,567 crore for capital expenditure, with investments planned in roads, railways, airports, industrial land, reliable power supply, Metro expansion and the Bengaluru Suburban Rail project. He also said nearly 70% of Karnataka’s installed power capacity came from renewable sources, adding that govt was expanding solar and wind generation and focusing on energy storage. “We want Karnataka to be not just an industrial hub, but a clean industrial hub,” he said.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru’s Jakkarayanakere may return to public use as playground
briefs.bodyText:
Nestled between a grown residential neighbourhood and the city’s transport hub, Jakkarayanakere, a site steeped in history, is once again at the centre of plans for transformation. The site was once a lake, which has lost all characters of a waterbody decades ago and was being used as a playground, before it was reinvented for Namma Metro’s casting work and later Bengaluru City Police.
The site is currently being used by the Police Department, which plans to convert it into a parade ground and police quarters. However, local residents are demanding that it be opened to the public and developed into a playground.
Discussions are under way between MLA for Gandhinagar Dinesh Gundu Rao and the Home Department, but a final decision is yet to be taken. Meanwhile, the department has cleaned up the land and undertaken plantation work. However, confusion over the subsequent transfer of the land after 2007 has led to a series of discussions to resolve the issue.
Paucity of playgrounds
Speaking to The Hindu, Mr. Rao said there was a severe shortage of open playgrounds in the city and that Jakkarayanakere, which was once a playground, could serve as an alternative for residents in the area.
Mr. Rao said the ground was originally used as a playground before it was handed over to the metro for casting works in 2007. The metro, he said, subsequently handed it over to the Police Department as compensation for land acquired elsewhere. The police then converted it into a dumping yard for seized vehicles.
“We have held meetings, and the Home Minister has said that alternative land for the police will be identified. The plan is to develop this into a well-equipped playground,” Mr. Rao said.
The residents said developing the site as a playground would provide much-needed open space, particularly for people living in and around Srirampura, Rajajinagar and neighbouring areas.
Compensated land
According to sources, when the metro required land near M.G. Road, it acquired the Police Department-owned B.R.V. Ground and compensated the department by allotting Jakkarayanakere.
In 2022, the Karnataka High Court directed the Police Department to remove vehicles from the premises of police stations across the city. Subsequently, the police shifted the vehicles to Jakkarayanakere, triggering public backlash.
The site also began witnessing frequent fires. In one such incident last year, nearly 100 vehicles were destroyed, prompting discussions on moving the vehicles back to police stations. Meanwhile, Mr. Rao intervened and took up the residents’ demand to restore the site as a playground.
Parade ground
The police sources familiar with the developments said the department did not have adequate land to establish the City Armed Reserve (CAR) West Division. There was also a need to construct residential quarters for police personnel.
“Many police personnel are unable to afford the rising rents in the city, and we need to create facilities for them. We also need a parade ground and space for the CAR. Jakkarayanakere would be an ideal location,” an officer said.
Mr. Rao said that at a recent meeting, Home Minister Priyank Kharge had agreed to explore the possibility of identifying alternative land for the Police Department elsewhere.
“We have kept Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) Commissioner M. Maheshwar Rao in the loop and asked the authorities to identify land for the Police Department,” Mr. Rao said.
Once a lake
Jakkarayanakere was once a sprawling lake spread across several acres. The lake gradually dried up, and with urbanisation, residential neighbourhoods and transport infrastructure came up in the area.
The site is also associated with one of Bengaluru’s worst fire accidents. In 1981, a fire broke out at a circus set up on the northeastern side of Jakkarayanakere, killing 88 people and injuring 174.
Over the years, the lake has transformed into dry land, with a portion of it now being used as a playground.

briefs.headline: Tejasvi Surya disputes Karnataka’s metro funding claims, says Centre bears 53% of project cost
briefs.deck: The BJP MP’s remarks come a day after Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said that Karnataka was bearing 84% of the total cost of Bengaluru metro projects
briefs.bodyText:
BJP MP for Bengaluru South Tejasvi Surya on Thursday disputed the Karnataka government’s claims over the Centre’s financial contribution to Namma Metro projects, stating that the Union government accounts for 53.35% of the total approved project funding, against the State’s share of 46.65%.
The BJP MP’s remarks come a day after Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Wednesday that Karnataka was bearing 84% of the total cost of Bengaluru metro projects, while the Centre was contributing only 16%. Mr. Gowda had sought a greater financial contribution from the Union government and faster clearances for pending metro projects.
Ahead of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s inauguration of the elevated stretch of the Pink Line on November 13, Mr. Surya released a presentation titled ‘Fact Check on Congress Government’s Claims Regarding Namma Metro’, challenging the State government’s assessment of the funding arrangement.
Citing the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited’s (BMRCL) approved funding plan for Phases 1 to 3, Mr. Surya said that the total project cost of ₹77,890.68 crore was divided between the Centre and the State, with the Union government accounting for ₹41,558 crore and Karnataka contributing ₹36,333 crore.
He argued that the difference in the two governments’ reported contributions arose from the treatment of foreign loans worth ₹28,958 crore arranged by the Centre through international financial institutions.
According to Mr. Surya, these loans were included under the Centre’s contribution in BMRCL’s approved funding plan but were attributed to Karnataka in the State government’s presentation, resulting in the 84:16 funding ratio.
The MP also pointed out that BMRCL is a joint venture equally owned by the Centre and Karnataka, with each holding 50% equity. He said BMRCL is the borrower of the foreign loans, with the Centre acting as a guarantor.
Delay in approvals
On the delay in approving Metro Phase 3A, Mr. Surya attributed the prolonged process partly to changes in the State government’s project proposal and the need for a revised cost assessment. He claimed that the Centre’s review reduced the proposed project cost from ₹28,405 crore to ₹25,999 crore, resulting in estimated savings of ₹2,406 crore.
He also questioned the State government’s handling of land acquisition, project execution, and cost escalations, citing findings from the Comptroller and Auditor General’s 2026 report.
Mr. Surya called for better coordination between the Centre and State, adherence to project timelines, and scientific urban planning to ensure the financial viability and expansion of Namma Metro.

Prof. Shetty served as the Vice-Chancellor of Bangalore University for two consecutive terms from 1993 to 1999. During his tenure, he made significant contributions to the academic and administrative development of the University.
He held a PhD in Electrical Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, an MSc in Opto-Electronics from the University of Essex, England, and a BSc in Physics and Electronics from the University of Madras.
From 1988 to 1993, he served as the principal of Karnataka Regional Engineering College (KREC), Surathkal. Between 2000 and 2003, he served as the Member Secretary and Chief Executive of the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA), New Delhi.
He also served as the Vice-Chancellor of the Central University of Karnataka, Kalaburagi, and was associated with Nitte Meenakshi Institute of Technology (NMIT) as an advisor.
Throughout his distinguished career, Prof. Shetty held several key positions in the fields of education, research, technical education, and university administration.
Bangalore University paid heartfelt tributes to the departed educationist and expressed its deep condolences on his demise.

stories.headline: FBI seizes $1.2 billion in crypto stolen from Binance in record $6.3 billion heist
stories.deck: US law enforcement has triumphantly seized or secured judicial endorsement for more than $1.2 billion in stolen cryptocurrency, associated with the historic $6.3 billion heist from Binance. This initiative is part of wider actions against North Korean cybercrime intended to support its governmental expenditures. Following the initial breach, officials were quick to freeze over $2.7 billion of the…
stories.bodyText:
The US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) said Thursday that US authorities had seized or secured court authorisation to seize more than $1.2 billion worth of cryptocurrency stolen last month from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. The recovery forms part of a wider effort by US authorities and private-sector companies to track down funds taken in what is regarded as the biggest cryptocurrency heist in history.
The October theft involved approximately $6.3 billion in digital assets and has been attributed by the FBI to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking group. The US government and private-sector partners have so far managed to freeze more than $2.7 billion of the stolen cryptocurrency. The Justice Department said it had obtained court authorisation to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion of those assets, reported AP.
The latest action is part of Washington's efforts to disrupt North Korea's alleged use of cybercrime to generate funds for its government and illicit weapons programme. US authorities have repeatedly accused Pyongyang of using sophisticated cyberattacks to steal digital assets and evade international sanctions.
How did the $6.3 billion Binance heist happen?
The incident took place on October 29, when hackers drained approximately $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from Binance wallets used to process transactions. The bulk of the theft unfolded in around 20 minutes, according to blockchain records analysed by cybersecurity firms.
The precise method used to breach Binance's systems remains unclear. The exchange initially suspected that a laptop had been compromised but later said its investigation had uncovered additional points of breach.
Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs said the attackers had compromised Binance's transaction-signing infrastructure, which authorises transfers and allows funds to be moved out of wallets. In simple terms, the hackers may not have needed to steal the actual wallet keys but instead gained control over the system that authorised the release of funds.
Binance had said its investigation was continuing, while its co-CEO Richard Teng assured users that losses would be covered through the company's Secure Asset Fund for Users and its own resources.
How were the stolen funds tracked and frozen?
After draining the wallets, the attackers attempted to move the cryptocurrency across different wallets and blockchains to avoid detection and prevent the funds from being frozen.
A significant portion of the stolen assets was held in stablecoins such as Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC. Unlike decentralised cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin and Ethereum, stablecoins can be frozen remotely by their issuers, making it possible for companies to block suspicious transactions when alerted by investigators.
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said the attackers attempted to convert hundreds of millions of dollars in stablecoins into Ethereum to move the assets beyond the reach of issuers. The firm tracked $325 million in stablecoin conversions into approximately $285 million worth of Ethereum over nearly 20 minutes.
However, cryptocurrency companies, investigators and law enforcement agencies began freezing funds within hours of the attack. Chainalysis said the first freezes began at around 5:14 pm Eastern Time on October 29.
The US government and private-sector partners have since frozen more than $2.7 billion worth of the stolen assets. The latest court authorisation covers more than $1.2 billion. Such cases generally involve forfeiture proceedings, in which the government files a claim before a judge determines who has a legitimate right to the recovered assets.
The FBI has attributed the Binance theft to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-backed hacking group accused of targeting cryptocurrency exchanges, decentralised finance platforms and investors to generate funds for the regime.
Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis said its investigators strengthened the link after observing funds stolen from Binance being mixed with cryptocurrency taken in a separate attack on exchange Bitget, which had also been attributed to North Korean hackers.
North Korea has repeatedly been accused by US authorities of carrying out cryptocurrency thefts to generate revenue for its government and circumvent international sanctions. The funds are alleged to help finance the country's weapons programmes, including its prohibited nuclear and ballistic missile activities.

stories.headline: Nvidia sheds $1 trillion in a month; Huang slips to 13th on Forbes rich list
stories.deck: Nvidia faced a sharp decline in stock value following CEO Jensen Huang's surprising resignation, igniting fears about its leadership stability. In just one week, the company's market value plummeted by nearly $500 billion, with shares now down around 30% from October's peak. Consequently, AI ecosystem firms suffered losses, while competitors thrived. Investors are now bracing for Nvidia’s…
stories.bodyText:
Nvidia shares plunged as much as 14 per cent during Thursday's Wall Street trading session after the shock resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang, extending a weeks-long selloff in the chipmaker amid concerns over the company's leadership and the future of the artificial intelligence boom. The stock recovered some of its losses during the session, eventually closing 4.3 per cent lower at $166.19.
The latest decline has dealt another blow to Nvidia's market valuation, with the company shedding nearly $500 billion in market value since the close of trading last week. Its shares are now around 30 per cent below the record high touched on October 6, wiping out more than $1 trillion in market capitalisation over the past month. Nvidia's market value slipped below $4 trillion, a level it had not breached since July 2025, reported Reuters. Huang has lost his spot in world's top 10 richest people.
The selloff marks a sharp reversal for a company that became the world's most valuable publicly listed business on the back of the global AI boom. Nvidia's graphics processing units (GPUs), which power artificial intelligence systems and data centres, made it a central player in the technology industry and one of Wall Street's biggest market drivers. 
Its shares had surged more than 1,700% over four years before the recent correction, while its market capitalisation had briefly crossed $5 trillion.
Huang's departure has also taken a toll on his personal fortune. The Nvidia co-founder, who had been among the world's 10 richest people, has seen his wealth fall sharply alongside the company's stock. According to Forbes' Real-Time Billionaires rankings, he slipped two places from eighth to tenth earlier this week. His estimated fortune subsequently fell further, pushing him out of the top 10 to 13th position.
Also read: 
Trump unsure woman linked to Jensen Huang was a spy; report alleges 3rd affair of ex-Nvidia CEO
The fallout extended beyond Nvidia to companies closely linked to its AI ecosystem. Nvidia-backed cloud computing firm CoreWeave fell 8.1 per cent, while Nebius plunged 18 per cent after cutting its 2026 revenue forecast amid delays in adding third-party capacity. Super Micro Computer also dropped 12%. However, rival chipmakers Advanced Micro Devices and Broadcom gained more than 4 per cent each, as investors assessed whether Nvidia's leadership turmoil could create opportunities for competitors.
 Nvidia is also due to report its quarterly results next week, with investors watching its revenue growth and outlook.
The turbulence in Nvidia also played out against a volatile session on Wall Street, although the broader market managed to recover most of its early losses. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% to 7,592.40, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 189.40 points, or 0.4%, to 52,297.09. The Nasdaq Composite also shed 0.4% to close at 25,366.09, after falling as much as 1.6% earlier in the session. Rising oil prices following US President Donald Trump's remarks on Iran added to market pressure, with Brent crude climbing 3.3% to $95.82 a barrel.

stories.headline: A2B sells majority stake to Bodhi Tree in $180-million deal
stories.deck: The deal values A2B at $350 million, says a source
stories.bodyText:
Homegrown food chain Adyar Ananda Bhavan, popularly known as A2B, has secured investments to the tune of $180 million (over ₹1,600 crore) from Bodhi Tree Systems, a firm co-founded by James Murdoch, the younger son of media baron Rupert Murdoch, and Uday Shankar.
The 50-year-old brand has shed a majority stake for this deal. An industry source said the deal values A2B at roughly $350 million, and Uday Shankar will serve as Chairperson of A2B’s new Board of Directors. Veda Corporate Advisers acted as the exclusive financial adviser to A2B.
Vishnu Shankar, from the A2B promoter family, confirmed the news and told The Hindu that the funds would be used for expanding into newer markets, both nationally and internationally. Currently, the food chain serves south Indian vegetarian dishes and sweets. Mr. Shankar said western India and Europe are among the key markets the company is seeking to expand into.
“We also want to expand our retail presence. And for this, we will be modernising our factories in Chennai and Bengaluru. We are also exploring the possibility of setting up another factory to cater to the retail and export markets,” Mr. Shankar said.
Founded in the late 1970s, A2B has a strong foothold in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, and a growing presence across India. It runs about 160 restaurants and sweet-and-savoury stores in India, with 32 overseas outlets in markets such as Singapore, the U.S., and Australia. It also sells packaged sweets and snacks through retail and online channels.
The company is headquartered in Chennai, and employs more than 15,000 people. A2B is Bodhi Tree’s third investment, after ALLEN Career Institute and JioStar.
Director of Junior Kuppanna, Balachandar R., said: “There is a treasure trove of value creation in private equity and capital markets for regional legacy brands. Haldiram’s and A2B have only scratched the surface. I foresee at least 100 listed brands in the food and beverage space in the next decade.” It may be recalled that Mr. Balachandar was the adviser to the Dindigul Thalappakatti 2019 deal. The hotel chain, which is famous for its biryani, had raised ₹260 crore from CX Partners, a private equity firm.

briefs.headline: Kia, suppliers plan $2 billion investment in second plant in Andhra Pradesh, targets 2030 production kickoff
briefs.deck: The investment is expected to create about 12,000 direct and indirect jobs, the ‌company said, after signing a memorandum of understanding with the State government
briefs.bodyText:
South Korea's Kia and its suppliers plan to invest about $2 billion to set up a second manufacturing plant in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, with production expected to begin in early 2030, the automaker said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
The investment is expected to create about 12,000 direct and indirect jobs, the company said, after signing a memorandum of understanding with the State government.
"India is central to Kia's long-term growth ambitions," said Kia India Managing Director and CEO Gwanggu Lee, adding that the expansion would help the company introduce new models and serve domestic and overseas markets.
The expansion comes as global automakers ramp up investments in India, the world's third-largest car market, to tap rising demand and expand local manufacturing capacity.
Japan's Suzuki Motor, the majority owner of India's largest carmaker by volume, Maruti Suzuki, in 2025 announced plans to invest about $8 billion in the country over five to six years.
Carmakers such as Toyota and Honda have committed to expanding their manufacturing ambitions in India as well.
Kia's new facility in Anantapur will manufacture models powered by internal combustion engines and electric motors, adding 200,000 vehicles to Kia India's annual production capacity of 430,000 units.
The proposed plant will be spread across 465 acres, including land for suppliers, and will take Kia's combined investments across its two Indian facilities, including supplier investments, to about $5 billion. The company works with both Indian and South Korean auto-component suppliers.

briefs.headline: India's Ola Electric quarterly loss narrows on cost cuts
briefs.deck: The electric-vehicle maker reported a consolidated ‌loss of 3.62 billion rupees ($38.66 million) ​for the three months ended September ⁠30, compared with a loss of 4.18 billion rupees a year ago
briefs.bodyText:
Ola Electric's quarterly loss narrowed on Thursday (November 12, 2026), supported by restructuring and cost-control measures.
The electric-vehicle maker reported a consolidated loss of 3.62 billion rupees ($38.66 million) for the three months ended September 30, compared with a loss of 4.18 billion rupees a year ago.
The Bhavish Aggarwal-led company implemented workforce restructuring, cut warranty expenses and tightened working-capital cost management in recent quarters as part of efforts to improve profitability.
These measures contributed to a 28.4% drop in second-quarter expenses to 6.39 billion rupees. Consolidated gross margin stood at 29.93% compared with 30.9% a year earlier.
The company, however, said it expects gross margin to reduce in the third and fourth quarters as its expands its dealer-store network, though operating margin is expected to improve meaningfully.
Ola Electric, once India's largest electric two-wheeler maker by sales, continues to face pressure on sales amid aggressive competition from peer Ather Energy and legacy automakers TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp.
The company sold 41,651 units in the second quarter, compared with 51,775 units a year ago, according to vehicle registration data, causing revenue to fall about 39% to 4.21 billion rupees
"Demand is no longer our constraint, supply is," the company said in its shareholder letter, adding that it is working closely with supplier partners to scale capacity and output, month by month.

briefs.headline: CAG to table first integrated audit reports in December, covering MSMEs and logistics

The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has adopted an integrated approach to auditing interconnected sectors and government programmes to provide a holistic assessment of their performance, with the first set of reports expected to be tabled in December, K.S. Subramanian, Deputy Comptroller & Auditor General (Human Resource, International Relations, Coordination & Legal), told reporters on Thursday.
The integrated approach seeks to move away from isolated audits of individual sectors and bring together findings across departments to provide a comprehensive picture of performance and outcomes.
“This integrated audit is happening in a significant manner and is producing very meaningful results because what happens otherwise is there would be somebody doing an audit of the railway part separately, say, what percentage of freight moves through rail,” he said.
“Somebody [else] will talk about roads but now in one report, we will have analyse everything for a holistic picture,” he added.
Mr. Subramanian said the first set of reports following this approach is expected around December this year.
Officials present at the briefing said the initial reports would focus on two key areas — ease of doing business, with particular emphasis on MSMEs at the State level, and logistics, bringing together the functioning of the Railways, shipping and road transport departments.

briefs.headline: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
briefs.deck: Officials stated that DISCOMs would be evaluated for their performance over a five-year period, following by transmission, generation, renewable energy and RDSS.
briefs.bodyText:
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.
The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.
Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Consumer satisfaction takes centre stage
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.
Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.
The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.
Integrated assessment
Discoms have been selected for the first phase given their direct interface with consumers and the cascading impact of their financial and operational performance on other segments of the power sector and the wider economy.
The CAG will also rope in the coal department to facilitate an integrated assessment of the sector.
Findings would be presented to respective state legislatures through State Audit Reports. Common policy concerns and systemic deficiencies emerging from these reports would subsequently be consolidated and submitted to the Union Ministry of Power for “consideration and appropriate policy interventions.”

briefs.headline: Life insurers’ new business premium rose 26% to ₹42,914 cr. in October
briefs.deck: The policies/schemes issued by the life insurers in October was lower at 18,82,243 (19,53,996).
briefs.bodyText:
Life insurers’ new business premium (NBP) rose 26% year-on-year (YoY) to ₹42,914.34 crore in October, even as the number of policies and schemes issued declined.
State-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), the market leader, reported a more than 31% YoY increase in NBP to ₹25,315.52 crore. While growth was across the product mix, the notable increase was in Group Single Premium at ₹19,113.40 crore (₹13,719.30 crore).
Private life insurance companies, numbering 26, logged total new business premium of ₹17,598.82 crore, registering an increase of 19.45% YoY.
For the seven months ended October, NBP was 21.39% higher YoY at ₹2,88,518.07 crore. LIC logged a nearly 21% increase at ₹1,69,662.16 crore and private players a little over 22% at ₹1,18,855.91 crore.
The policies/schemes issued by the life insurers in October was lower at 18,82,243 (19,53,996). However, for the first seven months of the fiscal, the number was 1.15% higher at 1,35,64,263, the NBP data released by Life Insurance Council showed.
According to Emkay Research, the life insurers’ retail APE growth was a muted 5% in October due to base effect. In October 25, the insurers had logged more than 19% yoy on the back of GST rate exemption-driven growth.
The insurers are expected to report 11-12% retail APE growth in FY27. “Overall, with the sector clean-up (new surrender regulations and the proposed commission reforms), we see the sector positioning well for a gradual re-rating once it starts delivering growth,” it said.

briefs.headline: Norwest to hike investments in Indian mfg, healthcare, tech after $4bn global fund raise
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: US-based Norwest has raised a record $4 billion fund, its largest in 65 years, part of which will be used to expand investments in India, particularly in manufacturing, industrial services and healthcare. It currently deploys $250-350 million annually in the country.
Norwest 18 takes the firm's capital under management to $18 billion and will fund venture and growth equity investments across technology, healthcare and consumer sectors in the US, India and Israel.
The firm has maintained steady investments across market cycles for two decades, said Niren Shah, managing director and head of Norwest India. "Norwest is currently deploying around $250-350 million annually in India, which is higher than the earlier levels of investment. Norwest remains very bullish on India's long-term prospects," he said.
While fintech and consumer remain core sectors, Norwest is increasing its focus on industrials and healthcare. It will pursue growth equity, venture, platform and buyout investments. "Industrials and Healthcare are becoming increasingly prominent in our investment strategy. Norwest will continue to remain a Multi-strategy fund and focus both on Growth Equity and Venture investments, while also looking to undertake more Platform and Buyout transactions," Shah said.
The firm sees opportunities in value-added and precision manufacturing and industrial services, driven by Make in India and global manufacturers' growing emphasis on quality and supply-chain diversification over cost alone. "Our investment approach will continue to be centred on Growth Equity, with a greater focus on Precision Manufacturing and Industrial services," Shah said. Healthcare and fintech will remain priorities, alongside venture investments in AI and deep tech.
Since launching Norwest 17 in April 2024, the firm has made over 87 investments and helped more than 30 portfolio companies achieve exits through IPOs and acquisitions. These include Indian listings Swiggy and Amagi Media Labs, US listings BillionToOne, MBX Biosciences and Omada Health, and acquisitions of Qualified by Salesforce, Veza by ServiceNow and Ouro Medicines by Gilead Sciences.

briefs.headline: 'Legend replaces a Legend': Trump wants Tim Cook to replace Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang
briefs.deck: In light of Jensen Huang's sudden resignation from Nvidia, alleged personal conduct issues have arisen. Donald Trump has proposed Tim Cook as a fitting successor. The Nvidia board swiftly acknowledged Huang's significant contributions while confirming his departure. Consequently, Nvidia experienced a substantial stock decline. Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO as the company begins its…
briefs.bodyText:
US President 
Donald Trump
 has brought 
Apple
's Tim Cook into the conversation around Nvidia's leadership, suggesting that the Apple CEO should replace Jensen Huang at the chipmaker.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump called Cook the only person fit to take over from Huang, who has resigned with immediate effect.
“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend! President DONALD J. TRUMP “
Trump's suggestion comes after Cook stepped down as Apple’s chief back in September after leading the Cupertino-based company for more than a decade. Trump also recalled his association with Cook, describing him as “an incredible guy” and saying their professional relationship began during his first term as president, when Cook approached him for help with an issue.
Nvidia's sudden leadership change
Nvidia's board announced on Thursday that Jensen Huang had stepped down as the chipmaker's president, CEO and board member, with the resignation taking immediate effect.
The announcement followed reports of two alleged affairs involving Huang. One involves a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing. Another report alleged that Huang had an extramarital relationship with a senior company executive who reported directly to him.
A person familiar with the matter said Nvidia's board had met on Wednesday to consider Huang's removal.
The company acknowledged the contributions of its outgoing chief, saying, “Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. Shares of Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies in the world, crashed in opening trade on Thursday as its CEO Jensen Huang resigned.
“NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” it added.
The board has named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO while it searches for a permanent successor. Huang, who co-founded Nvidia and owns around 3.61% of the company, is its fourth-largest investor. He will also give up his board position.
Huang's departure was followed by a steep fall in Nvidia shares during Thursday's opening trade. The stock dropped 13.09% to $150.98, taking the company's market capitalisation below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025.
The exit marks a major leadership change for the AI industry, particularly for Nvidia, which Huang transformed into a dominant force in artificial intelligence.

stories.headline: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni renews contract to stay on for third World Cup in 2030
stories.deck: Scaloni also confirmed that no one will wear Messi's iconic No. 10 jersey during the upcoming friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica — La Albiceleste's first fixtures since the star's official retirement
stories.bodyText:
Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni renewed his contract with the national team through 2030, putting him on track to become the first manager to lead La Albiceleste at three World Cups.
The 48-year-old Scaloni coached Argentina to the World Cup title in 2022 and a runner-up finish this year after losing the final to Spain. His previous contract was set to expire in December.
“After giving it some thought and discussing it with my coaching staff and those close to me, we decided that continuing is the best path forward,” Scaloni said at a news conference on Thursday (November 12, 2026). “We reached an agreement very quickly.”
Making historyScaloni is the most successful manager in Argentine national team history, having also won the 2021 and 2024 Copa América titles, but had cast doubt on his future following the defeat to Spain in July. Lionel Messi — who has been instrumental to the team's success under Scaloni — has retired from the national team since that loss.
“I am grateful for all the expressions of affection,” Scaloni said, visibly moved. “A huge part of the decision to continue was, without a doubt, the fans. I want to keep bringing them the joy they feel when watching the national team, and I hope that continues.”
If he fulfils the terms of his new contract, Scaloni will become the first Argentina manager to coach the squad in three World Cups.
“I have the same drive I had on the very first day — the same enthusiasm — and I'm happy to be able to continue,” said Scaloni, who initially took over on an interim basis in 2018.
In making the official announcement, Argentine Football Association (AFA) president Claudio Tapia said: “This is the best outcome for Argentine football; it's something everyone wanted — something we all wanted.”
Ushering in a new era
Scaloni will now oversee Argentina's generational transition following the international retirement of Messi and the inevitable departure of several veteran players unlikely to reach the next World Cup due to their age.
“An important phase in our process begins now; we will give opportunities to the youngsters who are pushing through the ranks,” Scaloni stated. “We need patience — they have enormous potential, but perhaps they aren't yet ready to deliver what the likes of Messi, Ángel Di María, and Nicolás Otamendi provided.”
Midfielders Nicolás Paz, Franco Mastantuono, and Valentín Barco, along with forwards Matías Soulé and Gianluca Prestianni, are among the rising talents set to take on more prominent roles.
“These young players need everyone's understanding,” Scaloni said.
The future of the No. 10 shirt
Scaloni also confirmed that no one will wear Messi's iconic No. 10 jersey during the upcoming friendlies against Uruguay and Costa Rica — La Albiceleste's first fixtures since the star's official retirement.
“We haven't decided who to give it to, and we won't until it becomes mandatory. When it does, we'll see who gets it,” the coach revealed. “When we finally decide, we hope it's for good — we don't want to keep passing the No. 10 around to different players. When we do assign it, we hope it goes to a player who can truly make it his own.”

Ruturaj Gaikwad made his first appearance of the series, while Ishan Kishan took over wicketkeeping duties in place of KL Rahul.
